RiskMap 2.0.0

RiskMap 2.0.0 is a redesign of the package. Many functions of 1.0.0 have been renamed, merged or removed, so code written for 1.0.0 needs changing. The table gives the replacement of each function of 1.0.0, and the main changes follow.

Functions of 1.0.0 and their replacements

1.0.0 2.0.0
assess_pp() assess_prediction()
assess_sim() assess_simulation()
check_mcmc() plot_mcmc()
compute_ID_coords() create_ids()
convex_hull_sf() create_convex_hull()
dast() Removed, to move to a separate package
dist_summaries() summarise_distance()
glgpm_sim() simulate_glgpm()
Laplace_sampling_MCMC() Removed, now internal
matern.grad.phi() matern_gradient_phi()
matern.hessian.phi() matern_hessian_phi()
matern_cor() matern_correlation()
maxim.integrand() maxim_integrand()
plot_AnPIT(), plot_score() plot() of assess_prediction() results
plot_mda() Removed, to move with dast()
plot_s_variogram() plot() of variogram() results
plot_sim_surf() plot() of simulate_glgpm() results
pred_over_grid(), pred_target_grid() predict()
pred_target_shp() predict() with boundaries
propose_utm() propose_crs()
s_variogram() variogram()
set_control_sim() set_control_mcmc()
surf_sim() simulate_glgpm()
update_predictors() Removed, give the predictors in the newdata of predict()

Main changes

Model fitting

  • glgpm() fits Gaussian, binomial, Poisson and negative binomial models. A link can be named in a family object, such as binomial("probit"), and any other link given as an inverse link function.
  • Non-Gaussian models are fitted by certified Monte Carlo maximum likelihood, which enlarges its samples until the Monte Carlo error of the estimates is small and reports a bound on that error.
  • In binomial and Poisson fits, household effects whose children differ in covariates are now integrated out, so such fits are much faster.
  • check_fit() reports how a fit was computed and flags anything that needs attention. profile() gives profile likelihoods and parametric_bootstrap() bootstrap intervals for the parameters.

Prediction

  • A single predict() method replaces the three-stage interface of 1.0.0. It predicts at new locations or over the areas given in boundaries, with exceedance probabilities, population weights, standardisation and, if asked, the uncertainty of the estimated parameters.
  • plot() maps predictions, to_table() tabulates predictions over areas, and assess_extrapolation() shows where predictions go beyond the data.

Data and projections

  • Data are sf objects with a coordinate reference system. propose_crs() proposes a projection that keeps distances accurate, and glgpm() uses it for data in longitude and latitude.
  • create_grid() builds prediction grids, also from the cells of a raster, get_worldpop() downloads WorldPop population counts, and variogram() gives the empirical variogram with a permutation envelope.

Assessment and simulation

  • assess_prediction() compares models by spatial cross-validation.
  • specify_glgpm() and simulate_glgpm() simulate data and surfaces from a model, and assess_simulation() assesses prediction targets on them.

Messages

  • Errors, warnings and messages are written with cli and have classes, listed in ?riskmap_conditions, and long computations show their progress (?riskmap_progress). options(RiskMap.messages = FALSE) silences the messages.
